newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 4.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- A retired Army four-star general who was accused of aiding the 1979 assassination of former president Park Chung-hee had his honor fully restored when he was aquitted of sedition on Thursday.

- The Finance Ministry and The Bank of Korea announced that an interest-rate liberalisation plan will be fully implmented on July 7, allowing banks to set their own interest rates on savings accounts.
- Subway unions in Seoul and Pusan voted to stage a full-out strike next Wednesday unless their demands were met in negotiations with management.
- Japan's seizure of Korean fishing vessels has poured cold water on the atmosphere for bilateral negotiations to revise a fishing agreement.

- Korea's automakers, reeling under swelling inventories and sagging sales at home, will likely face tought competition from foreign rivals, who resumed pressure to open the domestic car market wider.
